subject: Clinical-data residency windows & de-identification options — CardioSense inquiry
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@cardiosense.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Clarify storage windows & masking options for CardioSense PHI

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our security and compliance team is reviewing Redwood for a pilot and we need to confirm a few specific points about PII/PHI handling in the EU region before we move to procurement:

- Can you enumerate the configurable retention "windows" for primary request logs, model input payloads, and embeddings? We need maximums and minimums you can offer for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
- What redaction/de-identification patterns do you support out-of-the-box (field-level removal, deterministic hashing, tokenization, client-side pseudonymization)? Which of these are compatible with streaming and long-running chat sessions?
- How are deletions handled for backups and object-store snapshots? Our auditors require an answer about restore points and how long deleted PHI may persist in backups.
- For EU-region deployments, do you provide an auditor-ready attestation describing these controls?

Could you send a short technical summary + proposed mutual action plan for a pilot (30-day retention, EU private tenancy if possible)? We have a kickoff window next week for compliance sign-off.

Best,
Lina
Director, Security & Privacy
CardioSense Health

---
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@cardiosense.com>, CardioSense Security <security@cardiosense.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 13:46:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Clarify storage windows & masking options for CardioSense PHI

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (sales) plus Marissa (legal) and Laura (product) so we can provide a concise, auditor-ready response. High-level answers below; Marissa and Laura will add details and SLA language.

1) Retention windows (configurable per route):
   - Hosted API (default): request payload metadata retained 30 days; full payloads (when enabled) retained 30 days by default. Embeddings stored as long as the customer configures them (default: off). We can reduce the default to 7 days for some accounts via contract.
   - Dedicated: customer-configurable policies. Typical offer: 7 / 30 / 90 day buckets.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): retention fully configurable by customer; we can provide scripts to purge on-demand.

2) Redaction / de-id options:
   - Field-level redaction at ingestion: selectors (JSON path) to strip fields before storage.
   - Deterministic hashing/pseudonymization: we support reversible tokenization via customer-managed KMS for pseudonym mapping, and irreversible hashing if desired.
   - Client-side pseudonymization: recommended when CardioSense needs strongest assurance (no PHI leaves client).
   - Streaming compatibility: redaction before tokenization is safest; post-tokenization redaction is possible but impacts model behavior. For long chat sessions we recommend prefix/KV-aware redaction to keep cache coherence.

3) Backups and snapshots:
   - Hosted: primary deletion (writes a deletion marker) purges primary indexes within our standard SLA (7 days). Backups and object-store snapshots have a rolling retention window; default backup retention is 90 days but can be reduced to 30 days for regulated pilots via contract addendum. Final purging from immutable backup index typically occurs at backup window expiry; we provide an attestation of when snapshots containing the data will no longer exist.
   - Dedicated/Private: backup lifecycle is configurable; on-prem installs can be configured for immediate removal and are subject to the customer's on-site backup policies.

4) Auditor artifacts: we can provide SOC 2 Type II scope statements, deletion logs, KMS audit entries (if customer-managed), and a short attestation for the MAP.

I'm attaching a one-page summary and a simple EU data-flow diagram for context (see attachments). Marissa / Laura — can you confirm SLA language and whether we should offer 30-day pilot defaults for CardioSense?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redaction-options-summary.pdf, eu-data-flow-diagram.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@cardiosense.com>, CardioSense Security <security@cardiosense.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Clarify storage windows & masking options for CardioSense PHI

Lina / team — quick legal/compliance summary from our side. Short answers for your auditors: 

- Retention limits we can contractually commit to: 7, 30, or 90 days on primary stores for hosted and dedicated. For Private (customer-managed infra) we accept a contractual clause that makes the customer responsible for retention lifecycle; we still ship deletion tooling and a playbook.
- Backups: standard hosted backup retention is 90 days. For regulated pilots we will include a backup retention reduction to 30 days in the SOW. We cannot guarantee immediate destruction of immutable snapshots prior to their expiry date unless using a Private deployment model where the customer controls snapshot lifecycle.
- Deletion evidence: we can provide deletion logs, KMS key events, and an exportable audit trail. We will also produce a one-page attestation that outlines the deletion timeline and backup expiry window for procurement.
- Legal hold: if CardioSense requires legal hold for a subset of records we will place them on hold and exclude from purge processes; hold deactivation requires documented approval from CardioSense.

I'll attach our deletion playbook draft for your review — it describes primary purge, cache invalidation, and backup lifecycle in plain language. If CardioSense wants stronger guarantees (e.g., immediate removal from backups), recommend Private deployment for the pilot.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Attachments: data-deletion-playbook.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@cardiosense.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 15:10:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Clarify storage windows & masking options for CardioSense PHI

Technical notes to support the decision:

- Redaction timing: doing redaction at ingestion (before tokenization) gives the cleanest guarantee and minimizes leakage into model caches and embeddings. If the customer needs post-hoc redaction we can run a re-processor job but it has side effects on embeddings and may require re-indexing.
- Cache & KV state: long-running chat sessions keep KV caches across nodes. When an erase request is issued we enqueue cache invalidation jobs; typical completion for in-memory and on-disk KV purge is within 48 hours for hosted plans, but we commit to documenting the window per SLA.
- KMS & mapping: we support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS / HSM). For reversible pseudonymization we store mappings encrypted with the CMK; for irreversible hashing we never store mapping.
- API for erasure: we expose an Erase endpoint that accepts ids or selectors and returns an idempotent job id for tracking. The job writes deletion markers and records KMS events (if CMK used).
- Embeddings & retraining: embedding vectors derived from PHI should be treated as PHI; if deleted, embeddings must be removed from vector stores and any downstream indexes re-built. We will include a re-index estimate in the MAP.

We have EU region capacity in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and can provision a Private tenant for the pilot if CardioSense prefers the strongest controls. Happy to add a short appendix to the MAP describing the exact steps for purge and verification.

-Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
